prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and of its biologically active form, which established the basis for incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep a single-part prize on B010 naming Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The unanimity in round 1 is not what carries it, and the chair is right to ask whether it reflects independent judgement or anchoring. Tested on merit, the discovery chain is intact: Holst established incretin physiology and GLP-1 secretion and action, Mojsov identified the biologically active truncated peptide that gave the field a defined molecular target, and Drucker established proglucagon-derived peptide biology, receptor pharmacology and the therapeutic rationale. Large independent randomized programmes have confirmed glycaemic, weight, cardiovascular and renal benefit for more than a decade, so maturity is not in question. The citation is worded around discovery of the physiology and active form, and says that this made the therapies possible, so it does not imply that the laureates themselves developed liraglutide or semaglutide. That answers the chair's wording question: bridge to therapy by consequence, not by crediting the drug design.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weakness and I have not found anything in the supplied record that settles it. Knudsen's acylated long-acting analogues are what patients receive, and a discovery-only trio records that omission as a real cost, as the chair now says. Mojsov's priority on the active GLP-1(7-36) form relative to Habener and others outside the credited list cannot be verified from what I am allowed to read, and I should not claim certainty I do not have. A second part does not help: the candidates I find scientifically strongest for one are B031, with Mori and Walter as a clean pair but Ron and Kaufman omitted and a prospective clinical record, and B004, where Krainer and Bennett form a coherent pair but I am topically close to splicing biology. B052 and B048 have the unresolved credit problems the committee has described.

responses.point: The chair moved from Drucker, Holst and Knudsen to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, records the omission of Knudsen as a real cost rather than a clean judgement, and asks whether the third place should be Mojsov or Knudsen if Mojsov's priority cannot be supported.
responses.response: I welcome the chair stating the cost openly. I do not hold Mojsov over Knudsen because industrial work counts for less. I hold it because the prize is for the discovery that made the drug class conceivable, and the active-peptide identification is upstream of every analogue. On the chair's question, if the committee found that Mojsov's priority was positively undermined, which nothing in my permitted record shows, I would not automatically substitute Knudsen. That would change the citation from discovery to development. I would then prefer Drucker and Holst alone with a narrower physiology citation. Only if the whole committee wanted an explicit discovery-to-therapy citation would I accept Knudsen, and I would then drop the claim that this is a prize for physiology.

responses.point: Linnarsson called B031 the cleanest attribution case on the shortlist but a conceptual advance whose clinical consequences are still largely prospective, and said it is a stronger later candidate rather than a reason to change this year's configuration.
responses.response: I accept this. In round 1 I treated B031 as a strong alternative, and I still do, but I did not propose it as a partner to B010 and I do not now. Our first-round exchange, with Linnarsson, Perlmann, Wahren-Herlenius and the chair all placing medical consequence ahead of conceptual originality here, has changed my view that it could stand as a second part this year. I keep it as an alternative because the Mori and Walter pair is the cleanest attribution on the list, not because I think it displaces the incretin result. I also share his scepticism about B048: the trio we propose will differ, which shows the credit is not resolved.

responses.point: Perlmann argued that B031's medical impact comes mostly through disease biology and that Ron, Kaufman and Shamu are left out, and said he put BCL-2 (B005) above it because its arc to patients is more complete and the Cory, Adams and Vaux core is stronger.
responses.response: The omission of Ron, Kaufman and Shamu is the stronger objection, and I agree that no two-name credit describes the whole pathway. I still think the IRE1 branch and Mori and Walter's work form a defensible discovery on their own, but that is a judgement about credit, not about whether it belongs in a prize with an arc to patients. On B005 I see the same overlap with the 2002 prize for programmed cell death that he and Linnarsson raise, plus a four-name list with Tsujimoto and Korsmeyer outside it. It may be the better oncology-biology candidate, but I do not find that either of us has a defensible three-person set, so I leave it off my alternatives.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius said B052 (CAR-T) would be her first alternative, considers the evidence mature and growing into autoimmune disease, but notes that Eshhar and others designed early CARs and that Rosenberg's work is adoptive transfer rather than CAR design.
responses.response: I accept her point on maturity and that autoimmune use extends the modality's importance, and I said in round 1 that I would not call it immature. But with her own attribution reservations, I do not think B052 can be offered as a clean alternative. Any configuration within three names either keeps Rosenberg, whose contribution is adjacent, or drops him and leaves a pair that still omits the early receptor concept. I would rank it below B031 and B004 as an alternative for that reason alone, and I am open to reconsidering it if the committee finds a credit that names the receptor-design contributors accurately.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority on the active GLP-1(7-36) form is secure enough to name her, given that Habener's role cannot be assessed from the permitted record.
Whether the committee wants the citation to bridge to therapy; I prefer discovery with a consequence clause, but others may reasonably want Knudsen credited.
Whether first-round unanimity on B010 reflects independent merit or shared anchoring; my own merit assessment holds, but the shared fallback and credit reasoning show correlated views.
Whether a two-part prize is warranted at all, since none of B031, B004, B052, B005 or B048 has a settled attribution within three names.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for any shortlisted candidate. I work on RNA processing and single-cell methods, topically near B004 (SMN2 splicing), and I have co-authored with Linnarsson and Frisen, but no credited name on the shortlist is a documented collaborator or mentor. My disclosure is unchanged from round 1 and no member has requested recusal.
